ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: What part of the food web is the producer organism?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: This is a food web diagram, containing nodes such as Baby Atlantic Salmon, Kittiwake, Plankton, Krill, Gray Whales, Blue Whale, Humans, Spiney Eel, Killer Whale, Northern Bottlenose Dolphin, Squid, etc. Plankton is located in the upper right, and there are arrows from Plankton pointing to Kittiwake, Krill, and Squid; the diagram does not show Plankton obtaining food from other organisms. Reasoning: In a food web, producers are usually located at the basic position of the energy source and provide energy to consumers, and arrows usually point from producers to the organisms that eat them. Since Plankton's arrows point to multiple consumers, and it is not shown eating other organisms, the producer organism is Plankton.
